title: SEBI Demat 2.0: Tokenised Corporate Bonds Explained
description: SEBI has launched a pilot project for Demat 2.0, focusing on the issuance and trading of tokenised corporate bonds. This initiative leverages Distributed Ledg.

faq.a: Demat 2.0 refers to SEBI's pilot project exploring the use of Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) for the issuance and settlement of tokenised corporate bonds, aiming to modernise and streamline the Indian securities market.

These are digital representations of traditional corporate bonds, where ownership and transaction records are maintained on a secure, shared digital ledger (DLT) instead of a conventional central depository system.

faq.q: Will my existing Demat account change?
faq.a: Not immediately. The Demat 2.0 pilot is for tokenised corporate bonds using DLT. Your existing Demat account for traditional securities will continue to function as usual. Any integration or changes for retail investors would come much later.

faq.q: Can retail investors buy these bonds now?
faq.a: No, the current Demat 2.0 pilot project is limited to institutional investors and market intermediaries. Retail participation is expected in a later phase, after the successful evaluation and scaling of the pilot.

faq.q: How does this impact bond safety?
faq.a: Tokenised bonds are expected to offer the same investor rights and protections as conventional bonds, with SEBI providing regulatory oversight. The DLT itself adds layers of security through immutability and cryptographic encryption.

faq.q: What is the role of CBDC in this pilot?
faq.a: The pilot project is exploring the integration of India's Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), the e-Rupee, for the settlement of tokenised corporate bonds. This could enable near-instantaneous "Delivery versus Payment" (DvP) transactions.
